title: Scatter Graphs
summary: See how dots on a graph reveal trends so you can make sensible predictions from real data.

items.prompt: A scatter graph compares the age of a car with its value. The points generally slope downwards from left to right. What type of correlation does this show?

options.text: Positive correlation
No correlation
Negative correlation
Perfect positive correlation

items.explanation: This is negative correlation: as the age of a car increases, its value tends to decrease.

items.prompt: A scatter graph has revision time on the horizontal axis and test score on the vertical axis. What does the point $(6,24)$ represent?

options.text: $6$ hours of revision and a test score of $24$
$24$ hours of revision and a test score of $6$
$6$ students who each scored $24$
$24$ students who each revised for $6$ hours

items.explanation: The first coordinate is read from the horizontal axis and the second from the vertical axis, so the point represents $6$ hours and a score of $24$.

items.prompt: Which description gives the most suitable line of best fit for a roughly linear scatter graph?

options.text: A zig-zag line joining every plotted point
A straight line passing through the lowest point
A straight line that must pass through the origin
A straight line through the middle of the points, with roughly equal numbers above and below

items.explanation: A line of best fit should follow the overall trend through the middle of the data, with the points reasonably balanced above and below it.

items.prompt: The data on a scatter graph covers revision times from $2$ to $18$ hours. Which estimate made using its line of best fit is likely to be more reliable?

options.text: An estimate for $25$ hours, because it uses a larger value
An estimate for $10$ hours, because it is interpolation
An estimate for $25$ hours, because it is extrapolation
Both estimates are equally reliable

items.explanation: An estimate at $10$ hours is interpolation because it lies within the observed range. An estimate at $25$ hours is extrapolation, so the trend may not continue that far.

items.prompt: A line of best fit is drawn with practice time on the horizontal axis and score on the vertical axis. How should you estimate the score for $10$ hours of practice?

options.text: Start at $10$ on the horizontal axis, go up to the line, then go across to the score axis
Start at $10$ on the score axis, go across to the line, then go down
Use the score of the nearest plotted point
Read the highest score shown on the graph

items.explanation: Begin with the given practice time on the horizontal axis, move vertically to the line of best fit, and then move horizontally to read the estimated score.
